paragraphs.title: The Elders and Their Inquiry of God

easy.explanation: The passage says that certain elders of Israel came to Ezekiel.
easy.q: Who came to Ezekiel?

easy.explanation: They came to enquire of the Lord.
easy.q: Why did the elders come?

easy.explanation: The elders sat before the prophet.
easy.q: Where did the elders sit?

answers: He refused to be enquired of by them
He sent them into the wilderness
medium.explanation: The Lord said, “I will not be enquired of by you.”
medium.q: How did the Lord respond to the elders’ inquiry?

medium.explanation: Ezekiel was told to make them know the abominations of their fathers.
medium.q: What did the Lord command Ezekiel to make known to the elders?

answers: To seek an answer or guidance
medium.explanation: To enquire of the Lord means to seek Him for an answer or guidance.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “enquire” mean?

answers: It was not accepted as sincere
The Lord did not know about it
challenge.explanation: The Lord refused their inquiry, showing that it was not accepted as genuine.
challenge.q: What does the Lord’s response suggest about the elders’ inquiry?

answers: The present generation is connected with its sinful history
Egypt is connected with the holy mountain
The Sabbath is connected with sacrifice
challenge.explanation: The elders are addressed in light of the sins of their fathers.
challenge.q: What connection is made by mentioning the fathers’ abominations?

answers: They came as representatives of Israel
They had come from the wilderness
challenge.explanation: They are specifically called the elders of Israel.
challenge.q: What does the opening description emphasize about the elders?

short_answers.question: According to verse 1, in what year did the elders come to Ezekiel?
short_answers.answer: The seventh year.
short_answers.explanation: The passage begins by saying that it was in the seventh year.

short_answers.question: What did the elders do after coming to Ezekiel?
short_answers.answer: They sat before him.
short_answers.explanation: The verse says they came to enquire of the Lord and sat before Ezekiel.

short_answers.question: Whose abominations were Ezekiel to make known?
short_answers.answer: The abominations of their fathers.
short_answers.explanation: The Lord commanded Ezekiel to make known the abominations of their fathers.

paragraphs.title: Israel in Egypt and the Exodus into the Wilderness

answers: In the wilderness of the people
easy.explanation: The Lord says that He made Himself known to Israel in the land of Egypt.
easy.q: Where did the Lord make Himself known to Israel?

answers: A land flowing with milk and honey
Only the land of the nations
easy.explanation: The promised land is described as flowing with milk and honey.
easy.q: What kind of land did the Lord promise to give Israel?

easy.explanation: The Lord gave them His statutes, judgments, and Sabbaths.
easy.q: What did the Lord give Israel in the wilderness?

answers: Cast them away and not defile themselves with them
medium.explanation: They were told to cast away the abominations and not defile themselves with the idols of Egypt.
medium.q: What were the Israelites commanded to do with the idols of Egypt?

answers: So that His name would not be polluted before the heathen
So He could return them to Egypt
So He could abolish the Sabbath
medium.explanation: He acted so that His name would not be polluted before the heathen.
medium.q: Why did the Lord act for His name’s sake after Israel rebelled?

answers: They resisted God and would not obey Him
They followed God through the wilderness
medium.explanation: Their rebellion consisted in refusing to hearken and abandoning the Lord’s commands.
medium.q: What does “they rebelled against me” mean in this context?

answers: God chose and instructed them, but they rebelled
challenge.explanation: God chose them, delivered them, and gave them commands, yet they rebelled.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in Israel’s history in Egypt and the wilderness?

answers: They were a sign that the Lord sanctified them
They were given only to the heathen
challenge.explanation: The Sabbaths were a sign between the Lord and Israel.
challenge.q: What did the Sabbaths signify between the Lord and Israel?

answers: His eye spared them, and He acted for His name’s sake
challenge.explanation: The Lord says that His eye spared them from destroying them and that He acted for His name’s sake.
challenge.q: Why did the Lord not destroy Israel completely in the wilderness?

short_answers.question: What did the Lord command Israel to cast away?
short_answers.answer: The abominations of their eyes and the idols of Egypt.
short_answers.explanation: The Lord commanded every man to cast away these things.

short_answers.question: What did the Lord give Israel as a sign between them?
short_answers.answer: His Sabbaths.
short_answers.explanation: The Sabbaths were given as a sign between the Lord and Israel.

short_answers.question: Where did the Lord bring Israel after bringing them out of Egypt?
short_answers.answer: Into the wilderness.
short_answers.explanation: The passage says that He brought them into the wilderness.

paragraphs.title: The Children’s Rebellion in the Wilderness

easy.explanation: The Lord spoke to the children of the former generation in the wilderness.
easy.q: To whom did the Lord speak after the generation of the fathers?

answers: Walk in the statutes of their fathers
easy.explanation: They were told not to walk in the statutes of their fathers.
easy.q: What did the Lord command the children not to do?

easy.explanation: The passage says that they polluted the Lord’s Sabbaths.
easy.q: What did the children pollute?

answers: That the children walk in them and keep them
medium.explanation: They were commanded to walk in the Lord’s statutes and keep His judgments.
medium.q: What did the Lord require concerning His statutes and judgments?

answers: Pouring out His fury upon them
medium.explanation: The Lord said He would pour out His fury upon them in the wilderness.
medium.q: What did the Lord consider doing after the children rebelled?

answers: To disperse them among the nations
To gather them in one place
To bring them into the land
medium.explanation: To scatter them means to disperse them through the countries.
medium.q: What does “scatter them among the heathen” mean?

answers: Both generations rebelled and failed to keep God’s laws
challenge.explanation: Both generations are described as disobeying God’s statutes and polluting His Sabbaths.
challenge.q: What was similar about the sins of the fathers and the children?

answers: As a consequence connected with their turning to idolatry
As a positive gift of God
As the original laws concerning the Sabbath
challenge.explanation: The phrase appears after their rebellion and in connection with idolatrous practices.
challenge.q: How should the phrase “statutes that were not good” be understood in this passage?

answers: That they might know that He is the Lord
That they might forget their past
That they might serve the nations
challenge.explanation: The passage repeatedly gives the purpose that they might know that He is the Lord.
challenge.q: What purpose is repeated in the Lord’s actions?

short_answers.question: What were the children told to do with the judgments of the Lord?
short_answers.answer: To keep them and do them.
short_answers.explanation: The Lord commanded them to keep His judgments and do them.

short_answers.question: What did the children pollute?
short_answers.answer: The Lord’s Sabbaths.
short_answers.explanation: Their rebellion included greatly polluting the Lord’s Sabbaths.

short_answers.question: Among whom did the Lord say He would scatter them?
short_answers.answer: Among the heathen and through the countries.
short_answers.explanation: He said He would scatter them among the heathen and disperse them through the countries.

answers: Into the wilderness of the people
easy.explanation: The Lord says that He had brought Israel into the land.
easy.q: Where did the Lord bring Israel?

easy.explanation: They offered sacrifices, gifts, and drink offerings in those places.
easy.q: What did Israel do on the high hills and beneath the trees?

easy.explanation: They said, “We will be as the heathen.”
easy.q: What did Israel desire to become?

medium.explanation: The name of the high place was called Bamah.
medium.q: What was the name of the high place mentioned in the passage?

answers: It involved idolatrous and abominable practices
medium.explanation: The practices included idols, offerings, and other abominations.
medium.q: Why was the worship at the high places condemned?

medium.explanation: The idols were objects connected with false worship.
medium.q: What does “idols” refer to in this passage?

answers: Both show a turning away from the worship of the Lord
challenge.explanation: The desire to be like the heathen appears alongside idolatrous worship and abominations.
challenge.q: What connection is made between wanting to be like the heathen and worship at the high places?

answers: He refuses to be enquired of by them
He allows them to become like the heathen
challenge.explanation: The Lord declares that He will not be enquired of by the house of Israel.
challenge.q: How does the Lord respond to Israel’s request to be enquired of?

answers: The name continued to be associated with the place
The high place existed only in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The expression indicates that the name Bamah remained associated with the place.
challenge.q: What does “unto this day” emphasize about Bamah?

short_answers.question: What did Israel offer on the high hills and under the trees?
short_answers.answer: Sacrifices, gifts, sweet savour, and drink offerings.
short_answers.explanation: The passage lists these offerings as part of their worship.

short_answers.question: What was the high place called?
short_answers.answer: Bamah.
short_answers.explanation: The Lord says that its name was called Bamah unto that day.

short_answers.question: What did Israel say they would be like?
short_answers.answer: Like the heathen, or the families of the countries.
short_answers.explanation: They said, “We will be as the heathen.”

answers: The heathen will end His rule
easy.explanation: The Lord says that He will rule over them with a mighty hand.
easy.q: What does the Lord declare about His rule over Israel?

answers: From the peoples and countries where they are scattered
easy.explanation: He will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the countries.
easy.q: From where will the Lord gather Israel?

answers: They will be purged and will not enter the land
They will be sent to the holy mountain
easy.explanation: The Lord will purge them, and they will not enter the land of Israel.
easy.q: What will happen to the rebels and transgressors?

answers: In the wilderness of the people
medium.explanation: He will bring them into the wilderness of the people and plead with them there.
medium.q: Where will the Lord plead with Israel?

answers: Through the kings of the nations
medium.explanation: The Lord says, “There will I plead with you face to face.”
medium.q: How is the judgment described?

medium.explanation: Passing under the rod describes a process of examination and judgment.
medium.q: What does passing under the rod suggest in this context?

answers: He will rule even through power and judgment
The Lord will no longer act
challenge.explanation: He emphasizes rule with a mighty hand, stretched-out arm, and fury.
challenge.q: What does the Lord’s declaration of rule show about His kingship?

answers: To bring them to judgment and purification
To let them continue in idolatry
challenge.explanation: The gathering leads to pleading, examination, and the purging of rebels.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of gathering Israel from the nations?

answers: The rebels will not enter the land, while the faithful will serve there
Everyone will remain among the nations
The rebels will lead the people
challenge.explanation: The rebels are excluded from the land, while the following verses describe service to the Lord there.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the rebels and those who remain?

short_answers.question: Where will the Lord plead with Israel face to face?
short_answers.answer: In the wilderness of the people.
short_answers.explanation: The Lord says He will bring them there and plead with them face to face.

short_answers.question: What will the Lord bring Israel into?
short_answers.answer: The bond of the covenant.
short_answers.explanation: After causing them to pass under the rod, He will bring them into the bond of the covenant.

short_answers.question: Who will not enter the land of Israel?
short_answers.answer: The rebels and those who transgress against the Lord.
short_answers.explanation: The Lord says He will purge them and they shall not enter the land.

paragraphs.title: Worship of God on the Holy Mountain

easy.explanation: They will serve the Lord on His holy mountain in the land of Israel.
easy.q: Where will all the house of Israel serve the Lord?

answers: Offerings and the firstfruits of their oblations
easy.explanation: The Lord will require their offerings and the firstfruits of their oblations.
easy.q: What will Israel bring before the Lord?

answers: That the nations are their masters
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Ye shall know that I am the Lord.”
easy.q: What will Israel know when the Lord brings them into the land?

medium.explanation: The Lord says, “There will I accept them,” and “I will accept you with your sweet savour.”
medium.q: How will the Lord regard Israel’s worship on the holy mountain?

answers: The Lord will be sanctified in them before the heathen
They will hide from the heathen
They will worship the idols of the heathen
medium.explanation: The Lord says that He will be sanctified in them before the heathen.
medium.q: How will Israel’s gathering relate to the sanctifying of God’s name?

answers: An offering acceptable to the Lord
medium.explanation: The phrase describes worship and offerings that the Lord accepts.
medium.q: What does “sweet savour” mean in this context?

answers: The gathering leads to worship and the sanctifying of God’s name
The gathering removes Israel from the land
There is no connection between them
challenge.explanation: The passage connects bringing Israel from the nations with serving the Lord on His holy mountain.
challenge.q: What connection is made between gathering Israel and worship in the land?

answers: The land was promised by God to Israel’s fathers
The land belonged only to the heathen
The land was unrelated to God’s promise
challenge.explanation: The Lord recalls His pledge to give the land to their fathers.
challenge.q: What does the reference to the land promised to the fathers emphasize?

answers: God will be sanctified through Israel before the nations
The nations will worship their idols
challenge.explanation: The Lord explicitly says He will be sanctified in Israel before the heathen.
challenge.q: Why is Israel’s worship connected with the heathen?

short_answers.question: What is the holy mountain also called?
short_answers.answer: The mountain of the height of Israel.
short_answers.explanation: The passage calls it the holy mountain and the mountain of the height of Israel.

short_answers.question: What will the Lord require from Israel?
short_answers.answer: Their offerings, firstfruits, and holy things.
short_answers.explanation: These are specifically mentioned as things the Lord will require.

short_answers.question: Before whom will the Lord be sanctified in Israel?
short_answers.answer: Before the heathen.
short_answers.explanation: The Lord says He will be sanctified in them before the heathen.

paragraphs.title: Remembering Sin and Acting for the Sake of the Name

answers: Their ways and all their doings
Only the deeds of the heathen
easy.explanation: They will remember their ways and all their doings.
easy.q: What will Israel remember in the land?

easy.explanation: They will loathe themselves in their own sight for their evils.
easy.q: How will they feel about their evil deeds?

answers: For the sake of the heathen only
For the sake of idol worship
easy.explanation: The Lord says that He wrought with them for His name’s sake.
easy.q: For whose sake did the Lord act with Israel?

answers: Recognition of the evil of their ways
A desire to return to idols
medium.explanation: They will remember their defilement and recognize the evil they committed.
medium.q: What will remembering their evil deeds produce?

answers: He acted for His name’s sake, not according to their wicked ways
He acted exactly according to their sins
He did not act with them at all
medium.explanation: The Lord says He acted for His name’s sake, not according to their wicked ways.
medium.q: How does the Lord’s action differ from Israel’s ways?

answers: They will feel shame and rejection because of their sins
They will rejoice in their deeds
medium.explanation: The phrase describes remorse and contempt for their sinful conduct.
medium.q: What does “ye shall lothe yourselves in your own sight” mean?

answers: They move from remembering sin to recognizing the Lord’s action
They move from remembering sin to returning to idols
They move from ignorance to forgetting the past
challenge.explanation: They will remember their sins, loathe them, and know that the Lord acted with them.
challenge.q: What inner change is described in these verses?

answers: The Lord continues to act for His name despite Israel’s sins
The Lord stops acting for His name
Israel acts for the name of idols
challenge.explanation: The Lord again emphasizes that His actions are for His name’s sake, not because of Israel’s righteousness.
challenge.q: How do these verses continue the theme of acting for God’s name?

answers: God’s mercy does not approve of the people’s sins
God approves everything the people do
The people determine the Lord’s ways
challenge.explanation: The Lord acts for His name’s sake, not according to their corrupt and wicked deeds.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between Israel’s wicked ways and the Lord’s action imply?

short_answers.question: What will Israel remember in the land?
short_answers.answer: Their ways and all their doings in which they were defiled.
short_answers.explanation: The verse says they will remember their ways and all their doings.

short_answers.question: What will Israel do because of the evils they committed?
short_answers.answer: They will loathe themselves in their own sight.
short_answers.explanation: This is the response described in verse 43.

short_answers.question: According to what did the Lord say He would not act?
short_answers.answer: According to Israel’s wicked ways or corrupt doings.
short_answers.explanation: The Lord says He acted for His name’s sake, not according to their wicked ways.
